# 1 Enoch Chapter 27 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 27 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 27:1 — "unseeming words" vs. "unseemly words" vs. "blasphemies"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "utter with their lips against the Lord unseeming words" | "Unseeming" — archaic form of unseemly |
| LOGOS | "utter with their lips unseemly words against the Lord" | Standard word order; "unseemly" |
| PNEUMA | "spoke blasphemies against the Lord with their own lips" | "Blasphemies" — interpretive equivalence |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "unseemly words against the Lord." "Unseemly" preserves the literal character of the description without pre-interpreting it as "blasphemies" (which is accurate but interpretive). EMET's "unseeming" is an archaic form. LOGOS's word order is also more natural.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 27:2 — "spectacle of righteous judgment"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the spectacle of righteous judgment in the presence of the righteous for ever" | Literal; "spectacle" for the sight of judgment |
| LOGOS | "the spectacle of righteous judgment in the presence of the righteous forever" | Same, normalizes "for ever" |
| PNEUMA | "the righteous will look on as these cursed ones receive their just punishment" | Paraphrases; loses "spectacle" word |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the spectacle of righteous judgment." "Spectacle" (Ge'ez re'y, "sight/vision") is important — the righteous witnessing the punishment of the wicked is a key theme. PNEUMA's paraphrase loses this specific vocabulary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 27:4 — Enoch's praise response

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "blessed the Lord of Glory and set forth his glory and praised him gloriously" | Triple expression; "set forth" unusual |
| LOGOS | "blessed the Lord of Glory and proclaimed his glory and praised him gloriously" | "Proclaimed" for "set forth" |
| PNEUMA | "praised the Lord of Glory, declaring and celebrating his majesty" | Compressed to two verbs; "majesty" for "glory" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The triple verb sequence (blessed/proclaimed/praised) preserves the Ge'ez rhetorical intensification. "Proclaimed his glory" is clearer than EMET's "set forth his glory." PNEUMA's "majesty" departs from the consistent "glory" (Ge'ez sebt) vocabulary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
